title: Quantifying phosphorylation dynamics in primary neuronal cultures using LC-MS/MS
protocol: Briefly thaw frozen cell pellets in hand.
Lysate cells in lysis buffer (200 μL per 3 million neurons) by pipetting up and down using a mechanical pipette, repeating at least 15 times or until the solution is clear.
Add 1 μL benzonase to each sample and mix well by pipetting up and down.
Incubate for 10 min at room temperature (20°C–22°C).
Clear the lysate by centrifugation for 10 min at 13,000 × g at room temperature.
Transfer the supernatant to a fresh reaction tube.
Determine protein concentration in all samples accurately.
Prepare a standard curve using bovine serum albumin (BSA) in lysis buffer.
Perform BCA-procedure as described in manufacturer’s protocol.
Measure absorbance at 562 nm.
Calculate the standard curve using BSA concentrations.
Determine protein concentration of all samples accordingly.
Do not add reducing agents to the sample.
Avoid adding detergents; dilute sample below 5% SDS if necessary.
Work in technical duplicates and/or apply different dilutions of each sample.
Ensure protein concentrations are similar for all samples of the same preparation.
Adjust the protein content of all samples to 350 μg protein and prepare them in the same volume.
Dilute with lysis buffer if necessary.
Add DTT dissolved in lysis buffer to reduce protein disulfide bonds at a final concentration of 20 mM.
Heat and incubate for 5 min at 56°C shaking at 400 rpm.
Incubate an additional 5 min at room temperature shaking at 400 rpm.
Alkyte free sulfhydryl groups on cysteine residues with IAA dissolved in lysis buffer at a final concentration of 40 mM.
Incubate for 30 min in the dark shaking with 400 rpm.
Add 12% aqueous phosphoric acid at a 1:10 ratio to achieve a final concentration of 1.2% acid to the lysate and mix well.
Add six parts binding buffer to one part of the acidified sample (7:1 ratio) and mix by pipetting up and down a few times.
Add the mixture onto the spin column in 400 μL steps.
Centrifuge at 4,000 × g for 20 s or until all solvent has passed through the filter.
Discard the flow-through when necessary.
Wash captured protein by adding 400 μL of protein binding buffer and centrifuging at 4,000 × g for 20 s.
Repeat washing step for a total of four washes.
Discard the flow-through when necessary.
Transfer mini spin column into a new reaction tube.
Add 125 μL digestion buffer containing protease in a 1:50 enzyme-to-protein ratio to each sample.
Spin down the liquid briefly for 1–2 seconds.
Ensure that the whole filter is soaked in digestion buffer.
Return any solution passing to the top of the filter back again.
Remove air bubbles on top of the filter.
Incubate samples overnight in a wet chamber at room temperature.
Close the caps of all reaction tubes after incubation.
Do not centrifuge at step 14 to prevent pellet formation.
Repeat step 15 until all lysate has been loaded onto the column as needed.
Prepare a wet chamber using a microtube storage box with a lid and pre-wetted tissue sheets.
Generate a humid environment during digestion in the prepared wet chamber.
To remove chemicals that interfere with phosphopeptide enrichment or LC-MS analysis, wash peptides using C18 cartridges.
Add 80 μL of digestion buffer without protease to the filter unit.
Centrifuge at 4,000 × g for 60 seconds.
Add 80 μL of 0.2% FA to the filter unit.
Centrifuge at 4,000 × g for 60 seconds.
Repeat the previous two steps once more.
Mix the elution fractions thoroughly.
Condition the Sep Pak C18 cartridge with 2 mL pure ACN using either positive pressure or vacuum manifold.
Wash the sorbent with 1 mL of 50% ACN/0.5% acetic acid.
Equilibrate the sorbent with 2 mL of 0.1% TFA.
Load acidified peptide digests onto the cartridge.
Wash and desalt with 1 mL of 0.1% TFA.
Wash with 200 μL of 0.5% acetic acid to remove TFA before elution.
Elute the desalted peptides with 200 μL of 50% acetonitrile/0.5% acetic acid into a fresh reaction tube.
Repeat the previous step once more.
Take a fraction (5% v/v) and transfer it into a new reaction tube for screening of the total proteome.
Dry all samples in a speedVac at room temperature.
Split the yield of purified peptides to analyze the proteome (5% v/v of the digest) and the phosphoproteome (95% v/v of digest for phosphopeptide enrichment) before drying.
Resuspend the dried peptides in 150 μL of Binding/Equilibration buffer.
Vortex the sample briefly.
Spin down the sample in a tabletop centrifuge.
Ultrasonicate the sample in a water bath for 1 minute at room temperature.
Spin down the sample in a tabletop centrifuge.
Check the pH of the resuspended sample using pH-paper (at or below pH 2).
Dry the samples in a speedVac at room temperature.
Prepare stage tips with a 200 μL pipette tip and two disks of C18 material for each sample.
Dissolve phosphopeptides in 0.1% aqueous FA.
Vortex the sample briefly.
Spin down the sample in a tabletop centrifuge.
Ultrasonicate the sample in a water bath for 1 minute.
Spin down the sample in a tabletop centrifuge.
Condition the disks by adding 100 μL pure methanol.
Centrifuge at 2,000 × g for 3 minutes.
Wash with 100 μL of 50% ACN/0.5% acetic acid.
Centrifuge at 2,000 × g for 3 minutes.
Equilibrate with 100 μL of 0.5% acetic acid.
Repeat the equilibration step once.
Load phosphopeptides onto the tip.
Centrifuge at 1,500 × g for 5 minutes.
Wash and desalt with 100 μL of 0.5% acetic acid.
Centrifuge at 2,000 × g for 3 minutes.
Elute the desalted phosphopeptides with 75 μL of 50% acetonitrile/0.5% acetic acid into a fresh 1.5 mL reaction tube.
Centrifuge at 2,000 × g for 3 minutes.
Repeat the elution step once.
Dry the sample in a speedVac at room temperature.
Dissolve dried peptides of each sample in 15 μL reconstitution buffer.
Vortex the sample briefly.
Spin down the sample in a tabletop centrifuge.
Ultrasonicate the sample in a water bath for 1 minute.
Spin down the sample again in a tabletop centrifuge.
Transfer the samples into autosampler vials, e.g., QuanRecovery vials (Waters).
Inject and load 3 μL of the reconstituted samples on C18 columns using an Ultimate 3000 RSLC nano system.
Ionize the eluting peptides via a nanoESI source.
Detect the ionized peptides using a Thermo Scientific Fusion Lumos mass spectrometer.
Process raw files using the open-source software MaxQuant.
Assign a distinct sample name for each file indicating condition and replicate.
Download a sequence database for Rattus norvegicus from UniProtKB.
Import the downloaded sequence database into MaxQuant.
Set false-discovery rates to 0.01 on protein, peptide, and site level.
Specify a minimum of one unique peptide for protein identification.
Use a precursor mass tolerance of 4.5 ppm.
For MS2 spectra acquired in the ion trap, use a fragment mass tolerance of 0.5 Da.
For MS2 spectra acquired in the orbitrap, use a fragment mass tolerance of 20 ppm.
Quantify proteins using unique peptides for total proteome analyses in a label-free approach (LFQ).
Use at least two common peptides in at least three consecutive full scans identification for pair-wise ratio determination.
Assign variable phosphorylation on serine, threonine and tyrosine.
Analyse the phosphoproteome on the level of phosphorylation events using the “phospho(STY)site” output-table.
Analyse the total proteome on the level of proteins using the “proteinGroups” output-table.
